test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 15 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: August Kranti is also known as the _______ Movement.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Quit India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Quit India Movement, also known as the August Kranti, was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942 during World War II, demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• The movement was a mass protest involving millions of Indians, including significant participation from students, workers, and peasants.
 
• Gandhi gave the call for "Do or Die" in his Quit India speech delivered at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai.
 
• Despite the British government's severe repression, the movement marked a crucial turning point in the Indian independence struggle, galvanizing the Indian population against colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khilafat Movement**

 
 
• The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was a pan-Islamist political campaign launched by Muslims in British India to influence the British government and protect the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.
 
• It was initiated by leaders like Maulana Shaukat Ali, Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar, and Abul Kalam Azad.
 
• The movement also aimed to bring Hindus and Muslims together in the struggle against British colonial rule.
 
• However, it lost momentum after the abolition of the Caliphate in Turkey in 1924.
 
 
 
• **Home Rule Movement**
 
 
• The Home Rule Movement was led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant between 1916 and 1918.
 
• It aimed at achieving self-governance within the British Empire for India.
 
• The movement used a moderate approach, focusing on petitions and public meetings to build national consciousness.
 
• It laid the groundwork for more radical movements and played a key role in uniting Indian leaders and the public.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement**
 
 
• The Swadeshi Movement was part of the Indian independence movement and was a response to the British Partition of Bengal in 1905.
 
• It encouraged Indians to boycott British goods and promote Indian-made products.
 
• The movement saw the rise of nationalistic pride and economic self-sufficiency.
 
• It also led to the establishment of various indigenous industries, schools, and national institutions.
